Detailed scale computation inside the frequency tick from core and constant deltas and reference frequency.
Definitions and locking for frequency scale storage, reference and capacity queries, and scale-source registration.
Allocation, lifetime, and concurrency rules for the frequency-invariance CPU mask and per-CPU sample timestamps.
Semantics of AMU presence helpers, raw counter reads, and capability workaround checks.
Generic frequency-policy, idle, housekeeping, and hotplug interactions beyond the routed calls.
Full user-access window, exception-table recovery, and instruction-skip mechanics for trapped emulation.

findings.text: Frequency invariance tick and query are exposed for generic use: one hook refreshes the current CPU scale on idle entry and one query returns estimated frequency for a given CPU, both gated on AMU support.

Frequency invariance enablement proceeds from frequency-policy creation through per-CPU counter validation to mask allocation and source registration; hotplug online either joins a CPU to the enabled set or revokes the whole related policy when the newcomer lacks valid counters, while policy removal is intentionally ignored because counters remain usable.

Frequency query requires both enablement for the target and a nonzero reference scale, treats samples older than twenty milliseconds or on non-housekeeping CPUs as stale, then searches forward within the same frequency policy for a non-idle sibling that shares tick housekeeping, returning distinct errors for unsupported, invalid policy, and temporarily unavailable data, otherwise scaling reference by capacity.
Idle entry performs a conditional refresh only when the current CPU is enabled, performs tick housekeeping, and its last scale timestamp has already expired.
Paired activity-monitor sample carries two unsigned sixty-four bit fields, one for the core cycle counter and one for the constant reference counter.
Firmware counter identifiers use zero for core and one for constant.

Per-CPU counter readers store zero when the CPU lacks activity-monitor support, has the counter disabled, or is affected by the broken constant-counter workaround, and consumers interpret zero as an error rather than a valid sample.
Remote-capable counter read helper validates activity-monitor presence then either invokes the supplied reader directly on the local CPU or via inter-processor call with wait.
Counter reads under disabled interrupts must target the local CPU only; a remote target in that context triggers a one-time warning and permission error because cross-CPU calls are unsafe.
Collaborative performance control over fixed hardware exposes support probe plus single, paired, and write operations for core and constant counters.
Fixed-hardware support is reported when at least one present CPU implements activity monitors, accepting that reads for counterless or erratum-affected CPUs yield zero for downstream error handling.

Joint sampling reads the constant counter before the core counter to limit skew, extraction keeps only the descriptor bit window then shifts to zero base, and selection is by descriptor address matching the two defined identifiers.

Paired read rejects non-counter descriptors, maps unsupported hardware to a device-absent error to suppress pointless single retries, single read dispatches by address with extraction on success and unsupported otherwise, and write is unconditionally unsupported.
Emulation tracepoint group uses system name emulation with header guard and include routing through current directory file trace-events-emulation.

Thirty-two-bit condition evaluation derives each predicate from program-status negative, zero, carry, and overflow flags, with unsigned higher using carry set with zero clear, signed greater-or-equal comparing negative against overflow, and signed greater adding zero clear.
Condition dispatch provides sixteen entries in architectural numeric order, with the final two positions sharing the always-true predicate.
Unhandled-signal reporting is disabled by default.
Symmetric-multiprocessing suffix string is a leading space followed by capital SMP.
Two signal-forcing helpers report then deliver protection-key faults and bus machine-check errors with fault address plus key or locality detail.
Instruction-block state fields place low two bits at shift twenty-five and high six bits at shift ten, each with matching width mask.

User cache maintenance first rejects addresses beyond the user limit, otherwise performs the requested operation inside a user-access window protected by an exception table; clean-by-address variants are promoted to clean-and-invalidate, persistence and datapoint variants use their architected encodings, unknown operations raise illegal instruction, failures report segmentation fault and successes advance past the trapped instruction.

Trapped register reads return sanitized or live values then skip the faulting instruction: cache-type register hides clean capability and enlarges minimum line when the affected workaround is present, virtual counter and frequency either deliver signal when the per-thread trap flag is set or return hardware values, generic system-register reads delegate to the MRS emulator with illegal instruction on failure, and wait-for-interrupt is silently skipped.
Trap hook descriptor holds an exception-syndrome mask, an expected value to match, and a handler callback receiving syndrome and register state.

Sixty-four-bit trap table routes cache operations, cache-type reads, two virtual-counter forms, frequency, generic MRS range, and user wait-for-interrupt to their respective handlers, terminated by an empty entry.

Thirty-two-bit compatibility traps serve frequency through a single register and sixty-four-bit virtual counter split into low and high halves across two registers, each with its own terminated hook table, advancing by four bytes.
Exception-class name table covers all classes up to the maximum with a default unrecognized label and distinct human-readable labels for faults, traps, debug events, and system calls.
Overflow stack is a per-CPU array of unsigned words sized by dividing the configured overflow size by word size and aligned to sixteen bytes.
Bug-address validation unconditionally accepts, leaving rejection of stray breakpoints to the generic bug reporter and debug-monitor path.
Sanitizer exception bits use hexadecimal twenty for recover, ten for write, and mask zero F for access size.
